name: layout-composition-resolution
body: Layout composition resolution: `{{ template "<name>" . }}` is the standard Go html/template action over the library's layout namespace, not one of the six layout helpers (template-language). Its name is the library layout's file path — the layer root joined with the layout's path within its layer: `<layer root>/slides/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl` for a slide layout and `<layer root>/sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl` for a section layout. That path is the name the loader builds (`path.Join(root, layoutRel)`, loadlibrary.go) and the name render registers each layout under (`layoutName` / `namespaceForLayer`, render.go); it is the layout's path, not the template name. The namespace holds every layout text of the merged library, whichever layer carries it, keyed by that name and parsed with the executing template's own owning layer's function set (`namespaceForLayer` at render time, `exampleLayoutNamespace` at the load-time example check), so a layout invokes another layout in its own layer, a slide layout or a section layout alike, by that path name, and in a two-layer library a layout invokes a layout in the other layer by the target's own root-qualified path name (for example `{{ template "<external root>/sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl" . }}`). The example check resolves the name against the same library layout set render uses (example-layout-composition). A `{{ template }}`-invoked layout executes in the invoking template's own namespace, so its `media` helper binds to the invoking template's own owning layer; a `section` helper call is the composition that executes a target under the target's own owning layer (library-layer-references).
